 Malaysia, Korea apparel sales drive Misto segment growth
 FILA posted double-digit apparel growth in Korea. 
 Misto Holdings reported an 8.2% year-on-year increase in consolidated revenue to $2.85b (KRW3.8t) in the first nine months of 2026, whilst operating profit rose 29.5% to $462.2m (KRW 616.9b).
 For the third quarter, revenue grew 3.4% to $824.2m (KRW 1.1t), whilst operating profit fell 3% to $95.9m (KRW 128b).
 The Misto segment drove growth, with third-quarter revenue rising 15.1% year-on-year to $155.7m (KRW 207.8b) and operating profit increasing 8.6% to $7m (KRW 9.4b).
 Malaysia recorded double-digit revenue growth, whilst Korea's apparel business gained momentum.
 In Korea, FILA recorded double-digit apparel growth on strong sales of key products. The brand opened its first running-focused store, FILA RUNNING CLUB, in Seoul's Seoul Forest area. It also launched FILA PICKLEBALL CLUB at Lotte World Mall in September, featuring Korea's first pickleball court inside a FILA retail store.
 FILA also held its fourth WHITE OPEN SEOUL urban tennis festival, where new membership sign-ups rose 215% year-on-year.
 In Greater China, Misto Holdings expanded its in-house-designed products and optimised its store portfolio to improve profitability. It partnered with Korean streetwear brand MUCENT to open its first Taiwan store in September, with another location scheduled to open in December.
 The Acushnet segment posted third-quarter revenue of $687.5m (KRW 917.6b), up 1.1% year-on-year, whilst operating profit fell 3.8% to $88.8m (KRW 118.5b). Titleist golf ball sales increased in both volume and selling prices, whilst FootJoy improved profitability on higher golf shoe sales.
 Misto Holdings raised its 2025–2027 shareholder return target by 10% to up to $412.1m (KRW 550b) from $374.6m (KRW 500b). The board approved the revised target on November 11.
 The company also approved a third-quarter cash dividend of $0.72 (KRW 960) per common share, up 2.1% year-on-year, with total dividends reaching approximately $37.6m (KRW 50.2b).
 Ho Yeon (Aaron) Lee, CFO of Misto Holdings, said the company would focus on strengthening its core businesses, diversifying its brand portfolio and improving operational efficiency to sustain growth.
